item.title: Fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections
item.description: Fires in the U.S. are getting faster, larger and more dangerous, but people continue to develop and move into fire-prone regions. New research from the University of Colorado Boulder's Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES) shows that if we don't act on climate change, which fuels fires, manage vegetation or transform how we build and adapt to fire, the risk to structures in the U.S. will almost triple by midcentury. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Oxfam's Destroy and Rebuild Index: 'Wealthy minority of investors benefit from both sides of crisis'
item.description: The world's most vulnerable populations bear the brunt and the costs of the climate crisis, while the wealthy and powerful profit. Oxfam France’s Climate Inequality Advocacy Officer Selma Huart examines the relationship between concentrated wealth, unequal exposure to disasters and investors profiting from both polluting industries and reconstruction. “They are burning the planet, benefiting from it, but they are also benefiting from rebuilding,” she explains. Huart places redistribution at the centre of climate policy, calling for taxes on wealthy polluters to finance protection for… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Chile: miles de jubilados pierden sus ahorros tras la apuesta fallida de los fondos de pensiones
item.description: Más de 760.000 chilenos vieron reducirse sus ahorros previsionales, entre ellos cerca de 70.000 adultos mayores, tras las pérdidas registradas por el fondo más conservador del sistema. El revés se originó en inversiones realizadas por las AFP en instrumentos vinculados a las tasas de interés de Estados Unidos. La apuesta era que las tasas bajaran y generaran ganancias, pero ocurrió lo contrario: aumentaron, las inversiones perdieron valor y miles de jubilados y futuros pensionistas vieron disminuir sus fondos en torno al 10 %. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Ucrania: al menos 26 muertos en un ataque ruso durante una distribución de ayuda en Zaporizhia
item.description: Rusia llevó a cabo varios ataques aéreos el lunes 2 de noviembre contra una escuela que distribuía ayuda humanitaria en Komyshuvakha, en la región de Zaporizhia, en el sureste de Ucrania. item.title: ¿Qué se juega la democracia de Estados Unidos en estas elecciones?

item.title: Improved snow model captures Northeast's winter thaws and runoff more accurately
item.description: Mountain snow in the Northeast is different. The region's milder, more humid mountain climate shapes winter conditions that are different from those of the western United States. Yet, snow models don't always capture those differences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Arctic plant roots may play key role in climate change
item.description: A new review involving researchers at Umeå University has revealed the critical role that plant roots play in shaping how Arctic tundra ecosystems respond to climate change. The paper, recently published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, highlights how processes occurring beneath the soil surface could help scientists better understand how one of the fastest-changing ecosystems on Earth will influence the future climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: El exparacaidista británico Karl Bushby puso fin este lunes 2 de noviembre a su viaje de 28 años alrededor del mundo al llegar a su ciudad natal, Hull, tras cruzar a nado el Canal de la Mancha. item.title: Trump promised 'no more wars'. His foreign policy tells another story
item.description: Donald Trump promised an “America First” foreign policy and pledged to keep the US out of foreign wars. From the war in Ukraine and threats to Greenland and Canada, to the US intervention in Venezuela, Trump's shifting approach to the Middle East and war with Iran, Vedika Bahl examines his foreign policy record since returning to office. item.title: Historical records reveal the bitter truth about 17th-century Transylvania's climate
item.description: For roughly five centuries from about 1300, Europe experienced periods of unusually cold weather and extreme conditions collectively known as the Little Ice Age. Transylvania, a historical region in modern-day Romania, was also affected, but information about just how severe things were had been scattered in old town records, church logs, travelogs and administrative and monastic diaries. Fuente: Phys.org.
